name: Ezra

facts.author: Ezra, a priest and a skilled scribe in the law of Moses, who tells part of the story in his own words. Jewish tradition holds that he wrote the book.
facts.audience: The Jews who had returned from Babylon to Jerusalem and Judah

about: Ezra continues where 2 Chronicles ends. In his first year Cyrus king of Persia allows the Jews to go home and rebuild the temple of the LORD in Jerusalem (1:1-4). Nearly fifty thousand people return, led by Zerubbabel and Jeshua the priest.

They build the altar and lay the foundation of the temple. The people shout for joy, while old men who had seen the first temple weep aloud (3:11-13). Enemies stop the work for many years, but the prophets Haggai and Zechariah stir up the people, and the temple is finished in the sixth year of King Darius (6:15).

About sixty years later Ezra himself comes from Babylon with a second group, sent by King Artaxerxes. He had set his heart to study the law of the LORD, to obey it and to teach it (7:10). When he learns that many have married women from the nations around who worship idols, he mourns and prays, and the people confess their sin and put it right.

themes.title: God keeps His word
themes.text: The return happens as the LORD had promised through Jeremiah, and God moves the hearts of Persian kings to help His people (1:1).

themes.title: Worship comes first
themes.text: The first work of the returned exiles is to build the altar and the temple, so that they can worship God as the law of Moses commands.

themes.title: Faith under opposition
themes.text: Enemies accuse and hinder the builders, but the eye of their God is on them and the work is finished (5:5).

themes.title: The word of God
themes.text: Ezra studies, obeys and teaches the law, and calls the people to live by it.

themes.title: A holy people
themes.text: The returned exiles must keep themselves from the idol worship that had led to the exile.

outline.title: Cyrus's decree and the first return under Zerubbabel
The altar built and the foundation of the temple laid
